codes.name: Broad money
codes.description: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value (2016 MFSMCG).

name: Gender
description: This codelist represents the spectrum of an individual's internal and individual experience of gender, which can be the same or different from their sex assigned at birth.

descriptions.en: This codelist represents the spectrum of an individual's internal and individual experience of gender, which can be the same or different from their sex assigned at birth.

codes.description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a male.

codes.name: Non-binary
codes.description: An individual who defines themselves outside the binary of man or woman, and which may include various identities located at any point on the gender spectrum.

codes.name: Gender fluid
codes.description: An individual who does not have a fixed gender, and whose gender moves between different points on the gender spectrum. 3

codes.description: An individual who does not conform with the gender roles/norms/behaviours/expression expected from a given gender in a given society

codes.name: Agender / Gender neutral

codes.name: Gender queer
codes.description: Genderqueer individuals typically reject notions of static categories of gender and embrace a fluidity of gender identity and often, though not always, sexual orientation. People who identify as "genderqueer" may see themselves as being both male and female, neither male nor female or as falling completely outside these categories.”

codes.name: Indigenous gender-variant identities
codes.description: Individuals from indigenous communities who define themselves in a range of identities on the gender continuum outside the western binary approach to gender. They often define their gender from a spiritual perspective and are seen/see themselves as being able to cross freely between male and female, or to exist in a state that is in between, or neither.

codes.name: Two-spirit
codes.description: Two-spirit spirit is also used to refer to the 2SLGBTQ+ community, as indigenous peoples reclaim their ancestral ways of respecting individuals who do not define themselves within the gender social construct of man and woman.

name: REPORTING_PERIOD_TYPE
description:
It is used to identify and distinguish between different types of time periods in economic and financial reporting.  The specific start and end dates for a fiscal year (FY) can vary depending on the country, organization, or industry.
When reporting data using this codelist, it is essential to specify the exact start and end dates of the fiscal year being referenced.

codes.name: Current account balance
codes.description: The current account balance is the balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign.

By convention, lending fees on securities, gold loans, gold swaps, and crypto assets without a corresponding liability designed to act as a general medium of exchange are classified as interest and similar returns. codes.name: Imports of goods and services
codes.description: The import (purchase or barter) of physical, produced objects (goods) and services over which ownership rights can be established and whose ownership can be transferred from one institutional unit to another by engaging in transactions on markets by residents in one territory to residents in another territory. Imports reflect a change in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. The f.o.b. price (free on board price) of exports and imports of goods is the market value of the goods at the point of uniform valuation, (the customs frontier of the economy from which they are exported).  It is equal to the c.i.f. price less the costs of transportation and insurance charges, between the customs frontier of the exporting (importing) country and that of the importing (exporting) country. This indicator appears in other datasets published by the IMF. While every effort is made to ensure that estimates for the same indicator are consistent across different datasets, differences can occur due to differences in compilation methodology, reference year, splicing series to preserve time-series continuity, and when the data were collected, processed, and published.

codes.name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
codes.description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually  equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

descriptions.en: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). This is conceptually  equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

codes.name: Exports of goods
codes.description: The export (sale or barter) of physical, produced objects (goods) over which ownership rights can be established and whose ownership can be transferred from one institutional unit to another by engaging in transactions on markets by residents in one territory to residents in another territory. Exports reflect a change in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. The f.o.b. price (free on board price) of exports and imports of goods is the market value of the goods at the point of uniform valuation, (the customs frontier of the economy from which they are exported).  It is equal to the c.i.f. price less the costs of transportation and insurance charges, between the customs frontier of the exporting (importing) country and that of the importing (exporting) country. This indicator appears in other datasets published by the IMF. While every effort is made to ensure that estimates for the same indicator are consistent across different datasets, differences can occur due to differences in compilation methodology, reference year, splicing series to preserve time-series continuity, and when the data were collected, processed, and published.

codes.description: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).

descriptions.en: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).

codes.name: Direct investment
codes.description: Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with an investor (or its affiliated enterprise) in one economy having control or significant degree of influence over the management of an investee enterprise resident in another economy.

descriptions.en: Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with an investor (or its affiliated enterprise) in one economy having control or significant degree of influence over the management of an investee enterprise resident in another economy.

codes.name: Reserve assets
codes.description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). They can include monetary gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), reserve positions in the IMF, and other reserve assets. Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency.

descriptions.en: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). They can include monetary gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), reserve positions in the IMF, and other reserve assets. Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency.

codes.name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options

names.en: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options

codes.description: Financial derivatives are negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets.  Employee stock options are options to buy the equity of a company, offered to employees of the company as a form of remuneration and often at a discount to the market value. If the financial derivative is linked to a reserve asset it is excluded from the value of this indicator.

Employee stock options are options to buy the equity of a company, offered to employees of the company as a form of remuneration and often at a discount to the market value. If the financial derivative is linked to a reserve asset it is excluded from the value of this indicator.

codes.name: Unallocated foreign exchange reserves
codes.description: In the context of the Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves (COFER), Unallocated Foreign Exchange Reserves (FXR) is a residual category consisting of the difference between Total FXR sourced from the IMF's International Liquidity database and the total allocated reserves reported in COFER. It has two components: (i) the total FXR of nonreporting countries; and (ii) the discrepancy (if any) between the Total FXR of COFER-reporting countries and the total Allocated FXR reported in COFER.

descriptions.en: In the context of the Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves (COFER), Unallocated Foreign Exchange Reserves (FXR) is a residual category consisting of the difference between Total FXR sourced from the IMF's International Liquidity database and the total allocated reserves reported in COFER. It has two components: (i) the total FXR of nonreporting countries; and (ii) the discrepancy (if any) between the Total FXR of COFER-reporting countries and the total Allocated FXR reported in COFER.

codes.description: Foreign Exchange Reserves (FXR) are reserve assets other than monetary gold, SDRs, and reserve position in the IMF. Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. This represents the foreign exchange reserves that have been imputed by IMF staff.

codes.description: This code includes persons who have never been married or in registered partnership.

descriptions.en: This code includes persons who have never been married or in registered partnership.

descriptions.ru: Этот код включает лиц, которые никогда не состояли в браке или зарегистрированном партнерстве.
descriptions.pt: Este código inclui pessoas que nunca foram casadas ou em união de facto registrada.
descriptions.ja: このコードには、結婚または登録パートナーシップをしたことがない人が含まれます。
descriptions.fr: Ce code inclut les personnes qui n'ont jamais été mariées ou en partenariat enregistré.
descriptions.es: Este código incluye a las personas que nunca han estado casadas o en una pareja de hecho registrada.
descriptions.zh: 此代码包括从未结婚或登记伴侣关系的人。

codes.name: Married person
codes.description: This code covers both persons living in a same-sex marriage as well as in an opposite-sex marriage. This code excludes legally separated persons.

descriptions.en: This code covers both persons living in a same-sex marriage as well as in an opposite-sex marriage. This code excludes legally separated persons.
descriptions.ar: يشمل هذا الرمز الأشخاص الذين يعيشون في زواج من نفس الجنس وكذلك في زواج من جنسين مختلفين. يستثني هذا الرمز الأشخاص المنفصلين قانونًا.
descriptions.ru: Этот код охватывает как лиц, живущих в однополом браке, так и в разнополом браке. Этот код исключает лиц, находящихся в законном разводе.
descriptions.pt: Este código abrange tanto as pessoas que vivem em casamento entre pessoas do mesmo sexo como as que vivem em casamento entre pessoas de sexo diferente. Este código exclui as pessoas legalmente separadas.
descriptions.ja: このコードは、同性婚と異性婚の両方の当事者を対象としています。このコードは、法的に別居している人を除外します。
descriptions.fr: Ce code couvre les personnes vivant dans un mariage homosexuel ainsi que dans un mariage hétérosexuel. Ce code exclut les personnes légalement séparées.
descriptions.es: Este código cubre tanto a las personas que viven en un matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo como a las que viven en un matrimonio entre personas de distinto sexo. Este código excluye a las personas legalmente separadas.
descriptions.zh: 此代码涵盖同性婚姻和异性婚姻中的双方。此代码不包括合法分居的人。

codes.name: Widowed person
codes.description: This code includes persons whose marriage ended with the death of the partner and who are not remarried or in a registered partnership.

descriptions.en: This code includes persons whose marriage ended with the death of the partner and who are not remarried or in a registered partnership.
descriptions.ar: يشمل هذا الرمز الأشخاص الذين انتهى زواجهم بوفاة الشريك ولم يتزوجوا مرة أخرى أو في شراكة مسجلة.
descriptions.ru: Этот код включает лиц, чей брак был расторгнут смертью партнера и которые не вступили в повторный брак или зарегистрированное партнерство.
descriptions.pt: Este código inclui pessoas cujo casamento terminou com a morte do parceiro e que não voltaram a casar ou em união de facto registrada.
descriptions.ja: このコードには、配偶者の死亡により婚姻が終了し、再婚または登録パートナーシップをしていない人が含まれます。
descriptions.fr: Ce code inclut les personnes dont le mariage a pris fin par le décès du partenaire et qui ne sont pas remariées ou en partenariat enregistré.
descriptions.es: Este código incluye a las personas cuyo matrimonio terminó con la muerte de la pareja y que no se han vuelto a casar ni están en una pareja de hecho registrada.
descriptions.zh: 此代码包括因伴侣去世而婚姻终止且未再婚或登记伴侣关系的人。

codes.name: Divorced person
codes.description: This code includes persons whose marriage ended with a divorce procedure and who are not remarried or in a registered partnership.

descriptions.en: This code includes persons whose marriage ended with a divorce procedure and who are not remarried or in a registered partnership.
descriptions.ar: يشمل هذا الرمز الأشخاص الذين انتهى زواجهم بإجراءات الطلاق ولم يتزوجوا مرة أخرى أو في شراكة مسجلة.

descriptions.ja: このコードには、離婚手続きにより婚姻が終了し、再婚または登録パートナーシップをしていない人が含まれます。
descriptions.fr: Ce code inclut les personnes dont le mariage a pris fin par une procédure de divorce et qui ne sont pas remariées ou en partenariat enregistré.
descriptions.es: Este código incluye a las personas cuyo matrimonio terminó con un procedimiento de divorcio y que no se han vuelto a casar ni están en una pareja de hecho registrada.
descriptions.zh: 此代码包括因离婚程序而婚姻终止且未再婚或登记伴侣关系的人。

names.ru: Лицо, состоящее в законном раздельном проживании
names.ja: 法的に別居している人

codes.description: This code includes persons who are separated: they are still married, but "officially" separated.

descriptions.en: This code includes persons who are separated: they are still married, but "officially" separated.
descriptions.ar: يشمل هذا الرمز الأشخاص المنفصلين: فهم ما زالوا متزوجين، لكنهم منفصلون "رسميًا".
descriptions.ru: Этот код включает лиц, которые находятся в разводе: они все еще состоят в браке, но "официально" разлучены.
descriptions.pt: Este código inclui pessoas que estão separadas: ainda estão casadas, mas "oficialmente" separadas.
descriptions.ja: このコードには、別居している人が含まれます。彼らはまだ結婚していますが、「公式に」別居しています。
descriptions.fr: Ce code inclut les personnes séparées : elles sont toujours mariées, mais séparées « officiellement ».
descriptions.es: Este código incluye a las personas que están separadas: todavía están casadas, pero "oficialmente" separadas.
descriptions.zh: 此代码包括分居的人：他们仍然结婚，但“正式”分居。

codes.name: Person in registered partnership

names.ja: 登録されたパートナーシップの関係にある人

codes.description: This code covers both persons living in an opposite-sex registered partnership as well as in a same-sex registered partnership. Registered partnerships also include customary unions that are legal and binding under national law. This code excludes persons whose registered partnership was legally dissolved.

descriptions.en: This code covers both persons living in an opposite-sex registered partnership as well as in a same-sex registered partnership. Registered partnerships also include customary unions that are legal and binding under national law. This code excludes persons whose registered partnership was legally dissolved.
descriptions.ar: يشمل هذا الرمز الأشخاص الذين يعيشون في شراكة مسجلة من جنسين مختلفين وكذلك في شراكة مسجلة من نفس الجنس. تشمل الشراكات المسجلة أيضًا الزيجات العرفية التي تعتبر قانونية وملزمة بموجب القانون الوطني. يستثني هذا الرمز الأشخاص الذين تم حل شراكتهم المسجلة بشكل قانوني.
descriptions.ru: Этот код охватывает как лиц, живущих в зарегистрированном партнерстве с лицом противоположного пола, так и в зарегистрированном партнерстве с лицом того же пола. Зарегистрированные партнерства также включают традиционные союзы, которые являются законными и обязательными в соответствии с национальным законодательством. Этот код исключает лиц, чье зарегистрированное партнерство было юридически расторгнуто.
descriptions.pt: Este código abrange tanto as pessoas que vivem em união de facto registrada entre pessoas de sexo diferente como as que vivem em união de facto registrada entre pessoas do mesmo sexo. As uniões de facto registradas também incluem as uniões consuetudinárias que são legais e vinculativas ao abrigo da lei nacional. Este código exclui as pessoas cuja união de facto registrada foi legalmente dissolvida.
descriptions.ja: このコードは、異性登録パートナーシップと、同性登録パートナーシップの両方の当事者を対象としています。登録パートナーシップには、国内法で合法かつ拘束力のある慣習的な組合も含まれます。このコードは、登録パートナーシップが法的に解消された人を除外します。
descriptions.fr: Ce code couvre les personnes vivant dans un partenariat enregistré hétérosexuel ainsi que dans un partenariat enregistré homosexuel. Les partenariats enregistrés comprennent également les unions coutumières qui sont légales et contraignantes en vertu du droit national. Ce code exclut les personnes dont le partenariat enregistré a été légalement dissous.
descriptions.es: Este código cubre tanto a las personas que viven en una pareja de hecho registrada entre personas de distinto sexo como a las que viven en una pareja de hecho registrada entre personas del mismo sexo. Las parejas de hecho registradas también incluyen las uniones consuetudinarias que son legales y vinculantes en virtud del derecho nacional. Este código excluye a las personas cuya pareja de hecho registrada se disolvió legalmente.
descriptions.zh: 此代码涵盖异性登记伴侣关系和同性登记伴侣关系中的双方。登记伴侣关系还包括根据国家法律具有法律约束力的习惯结合。此代码不包括登记伴侣关系已合法解除的人。

codes.name: IMF Quota
codes.description: Refers to the financial contribution made by a member country to the IMF as a part of its membership in the organization. It consists of two components. i) foreign exchange component (25 percent) which a member is required to pay in SDRs or in foreign currencies acceptable to the IMF; and ii) domestic currency component (75 percent) which is payable in the member’s own currency at a designated depository, normally the member’s central bank.

descriptions.en: Refers to the financial contribution made by a member country to the IMF as a part of its membership in the organization. It consists of two components. i) foreign exchange component (25 percent) which a member is required to pay in SDRs or in foreign currencies acceptable to the IMF; and ii) domestic currency component (75 percent) which is payable in the member’s own currency at a designated depository, normally the member’s central bank.

codes.name: Reserve tranche position

descriptions.en: Reserve tranche position in the IMF represents the member’s unconditional drawing right on the IMF, created by the foreign exchange portion of the quota subscription, plus increases (decreases) through the IMF’s sale (repurchase) of the members’ currency to meet the demand for use of IMF resources by other members in need of balance of payments financing.

name: Transformation
description: This codelist represents a set of codes identifying the specific transformations or calculations applied to source data to derive new data elements or indicators. A transformation involves a computation with one or more input values (either base variables obtained by observation or derived variables from prior transformations) that results in a single output value (the value of a new derived variable).

descriptions.en: This codelist represents a set of codes identifying the specific transformations or calculations applied to source data to derive new data elements or indicators. A transformation involves a computation with one or more input values (either base variables obtained by observation or derived variables from prior transformations) that results in a single output value (the value of a new derived variable).

codes.name: Percent, 1 decimal
codes.description: This refers to a percentage value that is expressed with one digit after the decimal point, providing a level of precision to the tenths place (e.g., 23.4%).

descriptions.en: This refers to a percentage value that is expressed with one digit after the decimal point, providing a level of precision to the tenths place (e.g., 23.4%).

codes.name: 12-month moving average
codes.description: A moving average is a method for smoothing time series by calculating the average of the most recent 12 consecutive months of observations. Each new month, the oldest value is dropped and the newest value is added, producing a continuously updated average.

descriptions.en: A moving average is a method for smoothing time series by calculating the average of the most recent 12 consecutive months of observations. Each new month, the oldest value is dropped and the newest value is added, producing a continuously updated average.

codes.name: 12-month rolling beta
codes.description: A 12-month rolling beta is a statistical measure that shows the volatility of an investment compared to a benchmark index (like the S&P 500) over a 12-month period. This calculation is done continuously, with each new month's data replacing the oldest month in the calculation, creating a "rolling" effect. One unit is equivalent to one standard deviation of the standardized variable.

descriptions.en: A 12-month rolling beta is a statistical measure that shows the volatility of an investment compared to a benchmark index (like the S&P 500) over a 12-month period. This calculation is done continuously, with each new month's data replacing the oldest month in the calculation, creating a "rolling" effect. One unit is equivalent to one standard deviation of the standardized variable.

codes.name: 12-period cumulated sum
codes.description: A 12-period cumulated sum is a transformation that calculates the sum of values over the most recent twelve consecutive periods. The calculation is updated each period by adding the newest observation and removing the oldest, producing a rolling cumulative total.

descriptions.en: A 12-period cumulated sum is a transformation that calculates the sum of values over the most recent twelve consecutive periods. The calculation is updated each period by adding the newest observation and removing the oldest, producing a rolling cumulative total.

codes.name: 12-period moving average
codes.description: A 12-period moving average is a transformation that calculates the arithmetic mean of a variable over the most recent twelve consecutive periods. The calculation is updated each period by including the latest observation and excluding the oldest, resulting in a rolling average

codes.description: The first quartile (Q1) is the value below which 25 percent of the observations in a distribution fall. It represents the lower boundary of the second quarter of the ordered data and is a measure of dispersion and position.

The IMF's accounting records provide a standardized framework for recording and reporting economic transactions between countries, and using these records helps ensure comparability and reliability of data across different nations.

codes.name: Herfindahl index
codes.description: The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) is a commonly used measure of market concentration. It is calculated by squaring the market share of each firm competing in a market and then summing the resulting numbers. The HHI can range from 0 to 10,000. A market with an HHI of less than 1,500 is considered to be a competitive marketplace, an HHI of 1,500 to 2,500 to be a moderately concentrated marketplace, and an HHI of 2,500 or greater to be a highly concentrated marketplace.

codes.name: Imports of environmental goods
codes.description: Imports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods entering the national territory. A relatively high share of environmental goods imports indicates that an economy purchases a significant share of environmental goods from other economies. Exports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods leaving the national territory. A relatively high share of environmental goods exports indicates that an economy produces and sells a significant share of environmental goods to other economies. An economy’s environmental goods trade balance is the difference between its exports and imports of environmental goods.

codes.name: Capital account
codes.description: The capital account records acquisitions and disposals of non-financial assets as a result of transactions with other units, internal bookkeeping transactions linked to production (such as changes in inventories and depreciation) and the redistribution of wealth by means of capital transfers. In the context of the external accounts, the capital account shows (a) capital transfers receivable and payable between residents and nonresidents and (b) the acquisition and disposal of nonproduced, nonfinancial assets between residents and nonresidents.

descriptions.en: The capital account records acquisitions and disposals of non-financial assets as a result of transactions with other units, internal bookkeeping transactions linked to production (such as changes in inventories and depreciation) and the redistribution of wealth by means of capital transfers. codes.name: Capital and financial account

The financial account records all transactions in financial assets and liabilities. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included.

name: Prices
description: This codelist represents different types of prices or price adjustments, including those that have been adjusted for inflation (real or constant prices) and those that have not (nominal or current prices). It also includes various methods for adjusting prices for inflation, such as using deflators or converting to a constant base period.

name: Observation Status
description: This codelist indicates the status of an observation within a dataset, such as whether it is a provisional value, an estimated value, a final figure, or a value where a time series break occurs. (Source: SDMX)

descriptions.en: This codelist indicates the status of an observation within a dataset, such as whether it is a provisional value, an estimated value, a final figure, or a value where a time series break occurs. (Source: SDMX)

codes.name: Normal value
codes.description: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

descriptions.en: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

codes.name: Time series break
codes.description: Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).

descriptions.en: Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).

codes.name: Definition differs
codes.description: Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

descriptions.en: Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

codes.name: Estimated value
codes.description: Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

descriptions.en: Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

codes.name: Forecast value
codes.description: Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).

descriptions.en: Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).

codes.name: Experimental value
codes.description: Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

descriptions.en: Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

codes.name: Data included in another category
codes.description: This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

descriptions.en: This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

codes.name: Includes data from another category
codes.description: This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

descriptions.en: This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

codes.name: Missing value
codes.description: This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

descriptions.en: This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

codes.name: Missing value; data cannot exist
codes.description: Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

descriptions.en: Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

codes.name: Provisional value
codes.description: An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.

descriptions.en: An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.

codes.name: Strike and other special events
codes.description: Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

descriptions.en: Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

codes.name: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

names.en: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

codes.description: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.

descriptions.en: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.

codes.name: Missing value; holiday or weekend
codes.description: Used in some daily data flows.

descriptions.en: Used in some daily data flows.

codes.name: Missing value; suppressed
codes.description: Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

descriptions.en: Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

codes.name: Derogation
codes.description: Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.

descriptions.en: Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.

codes.name: Not significant
codes.description: Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).

descriptions.en: Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).

codes.name: Low reliability
codes.description: This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.

descriptions.en: This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.

codes.name: Unvalidated value
codes.description: Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.

descriptions.en: Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.

codes.name: Derived value
codes.description: A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

descriptions.en: A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

codes.name: Value imputed
codes.description: A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".

descriptions.en: A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".

codes.name: Derived from counterpart country data
codes.description: Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.

descriptions.en: Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.

codes.name: Unknown
codes.description: This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

descriptions.en: This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

codes.name: Observation status unavailable from external organisation

names.en: Observation status unavailable from external organisation

codes.description: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. Implementers should use attributes at the observation-level or at a higher-level such as: COMMENT_OBS, DATA_SOURCE or NATURE, to provide information on the source or nature.

descriptions.en: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. codes.name: Excludes one or more subcategories
codes.description: This code is used when data exclude one or several subcategories that it should normally include, resulting in under-coverage of the category. This situation typically arises when the category is an aggregate and code ‘K’ or ‘O’ applies to one (or several) of its subcategories.

codes.name: Budget balance
codes.description: The difference between a government's total revenue and total expenditure over a specific period. A positive balance indicates a surplus, while a negative balance indicates a deficit.

descriptions.en: The difference between a government's total revenue and total expenditure over a specific period. A positive balance indicates a surplus, while a negative balance indicates a deficit.

codes.name: Cyclically adjusted balance
codes.description: The cyclically adjusted balance is a measure of a government's budget balance that takes into account the effects of the economic cycle. It adjusts the actual budget balance for the impact of cyclical fluctuations in economic activity, such as changes in output, employment, and tax revenues, to provide a clearer picture of the underlying fiscal position. This adjustment helps policymakers assess the structural or underlying fiscal position of the government, independent of temporary fluctuations caused by the economic cycle. A positive cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural surplus, while a negative cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural deficit.

descriptions.en: The cyclically adjusted balance is a measure of a government's budget balance that takes into account the effects of the economic cycle. It adjusts the actual budget balance for the impact of cyclical fluctuations in economic activity, such as changes in output, employment, and tax revenues, to provide a clearer picture of the underlying fiscal position. This adjustment helps policymakers assess the structural or underlying fiscal position of the government, independent of temporary fluctuations caused by the economic cycle. A positive cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural surplus, while a negative cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural deficit.

codes.name: Cyclically adjusted primary balance
codes.description: The cyclically adjusted primary balance is similar to the cyclically adjusted balance but focuses specifically on the primary balance, which excludes interest payments on government debt. It adjusts the primary balance for the effects of the economic cycle to provide a measure of the structural fiscal position of the government, independent of cyclical fluctuations. Like the cyclically adjusted balance, a positive cyclically adjusted primary balance indicates a structural surplus, while a negative cyclically adjusted primary balance indicates a structural deficit.

descriptions.en: The cyclically adjusted primary balance is similar to the cyclically adjusted balance but focuses specifically on the primary balance, which excludes interest payments on government debt. codes.name: Expenditure
codes.description: Expenditure refers to the total outflow of resources, including payments, purchases, and transfers, made by a government entity during a specific period to fulfill its various functions and obligations. It encompasses spending on goods and services, wages and salaries, social benefits, debt servicing, infrastructure investments, and other government programs and activities. Expenditure represents the utilization of government funds to provide public services, maintain infrastructure, implement policies, and meet financial obligations. Monitoring expenditure patterns and allocations provides insight into government priorities, policy objectives, and fiscal sustainability.

codes.name: Total expenditure and net lending / net borrowing

codes.description: Expenditure refers to the total outflow of resources, including payments, purchases, and transfers, made by a government entity during a specific period to fulfill its various functions and obligations. It encompasses spending on goods and services, wages and salaries, social benefits, debt servicing, infrastructure investments, and other government programs and activities. Expenditure represents the utilization of government funds to provide public services, maintain infrastructure, implement policies, and meet financial obligations. Monitoring expenditure patterns and allocations provides insight into government priorities, policy objectives, and fiscal sustainability. Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually  equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

codes.name: Overall balance
codes.description: The overall balance represents the difference between a government's total revenue and its total expenditure over a specific period, typically a fiscal year. It reflects the net financial position of the government, indicating whether it is running a surplus (positive overall balance) or a deficit (negative overall balance). The overall balance takes into account all sources of revenue, including taxes, fees, and grants, as well as all types of expenditure, such as salaries, public services, and debt servicing costs. Monitoring the overall balance is crucial for assessing the government's fiscal health, its ability to meet its financial obligations, and the sustainability of its budgetary policies

codes.name: Personal income tax (PIT)

It is imposed by government authorities at the federal, state, and local levels and is typically calculated based on a progressive tax rate structure, where higher levels of income are taxed at higher rates. Personal income tax serves as a significant source of revenue for governments, funding public services, social welfare programs, infrastructure projects, and other government expenditures.

codes.name: Bank stock index
codes.description: A financial index that tracks the performance of a basket of stocks issued by banking institutions. This index provides insights into the health and performance of the banking sector, reflecting changes in stock prices of banks in response to economic, regulatory, and market conditions.

codes.name: Core consumer price index (CPI)
codes.description: A measure of the price level of consumer goods and services, excluding volatile items such as food and energy.

descriptions.en: A measure of the price level of consumer goods and services, excluding volatile items such as food and energy.

codes.name: Commodity price index, energy, crude oil (petroleum)

names.en: Commodity price index, energy, crude oil (petroleum)

codes.description: The Commodity Price Index for energy, crude oil (petroleum) is a measure that tracks the average price changes of crude oil over time.

descriptions.en: The Commodity Price Index for energy, crude oil (petroleum) is a measure that tracks the average price changes of crude oil over time.

codes.name: Commodity net export price index
codes.description: Represents the difference in the trends of export and import price indices for commodities. It is calculated by subtracting the Commodity Import Price Index from the Commodity Export Price Index. A positive value indicates that the prices of exports are increasing at a faster rate than the prices of imports, potentially leading to a favorable trade balance and contributing to economic growth.

descriptions.en: Represents the difference in the trends of export and import price indices for commodities. It is calculated by subtracting the Commodity Import Price Index from the Commodity Export Price Index. A positive value indicates that the prices of exports are increasing at a faster rate than the prices of imports, potentially leading to a favorable trade balance and contributing to economic growth.

codes.name: Commodity export price index
codes.description: A measure that tracks the changes over time in the prices of a basket of goods exported by a country. This index provides insight into the trends of export prices for commodities such as oil, metals, and agricultural products. An increase in the index suggests that the prices of exported commodities are rising, potentially leading to higher revenues for exporters.

descriptions.en: A measure that tracks the changes over time in the prices of a basket of goods exported by a country. This index provides insight into the trends of export prices for commodities such as oil, metals, and agricultural products. An increase in the index suggests that the prices of exported commodities are rising, potentially leading to higher revenues for exporters.

codes.name: Core HICP inflation forecast
codes.description: The Core Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) Inflation Forecast predicts the future rate of inflation, excluding volatile items such as energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco. This forecast helps in assessing underlying inflation trends and is crucial for monetary policy decisions and economic planning.

descriptions.en: The Core Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) Inflation Forecast predicts the future rate of inflation, excluding volatile items such as energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco. This forecast helps in assessing underlying inflation trends and is crucial for monetary policy decisions and economic planning.

codes.name: Commodity import price index
codes.description: This index measures the changes in the prices of a basket of goods imported into a country over time. It reflects the cost trends of imported commodities, including energy sources, raw materials, and food products. A higher index indicates increasing import prices, which may affect domestic inflation rates and the purchasing power of consumers, as well as impact the costs for businesses relying on imported goods.

descriptions.en: This index measures the changes in the prices of a basket of goods imported into a country over time. It reflects the cost trends of imported commodities, including energy sources, raw materials, and food products. A higher index indicates increasing import prices, which may affect domestic inflation rates and the purchasing power of consumers, as well as impact the costs for businesses relying on imported goods.

codes.name: Core PCE Price Index
codes.description: The Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index is a measure of inflation that tracks changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers, excluding food and energy prices.

descriptions.en: The Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index is a measure of inflation that tracks changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers, excluding food and energy prices.

codes.name: Consumer price index (CPI)
codes.description: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period.

descriptions.en: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period.

codes.name: Relative consumer price index (CPI)
codes.description: The CPI of the country compared to the trade-weighted CPI of the country’s trade partners

codes.name: Consumer price index (Urban)
codes.description: The Consumer Price Index (Urban), often abbreviated as CPI-U, is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.

descriptions.en: The Consumer Price Index (Urban), often abbreviated as CPI-U, is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.

codes.name: Commodity price index
codes.description: A commodity price index is a measurement tool that tracks the average price changes of a basket of commodities over time. These commodities can include various raw materials or primary agricultural products

codes.name: Deflator
codes.description: A measure used to adjust nominal values for inflation, reflecting the real value.

descriptions.en: A measure used to adjust nominal values for inflation, reflecting the real value.

codes.name: Flexible exchange market pressure index
codes.description: Measures the pressure on a country's exchange rate in a flexible exchange rate system, taking into account factors such as changes in exchange rates, interest rates, and international reserves. It helps in identifying periods of excessive upward or downward pressure on the currency, indicating potential stability or vulnerability in the foreign exchange market. Calculated as one unit equivalent to one standard deviation of standarized variable.

codes.name: Export price index (XPI)
codes.description: An index that measures the price changes of goods and services sold to foreign buyers.

codes.name: Financial stress indicators
codes.description: Quantitative measures that signal the level of stress in the financial system. These indicators can include volatility in stock and bond markets, widening credit spreads, and increased interbank lending rates. They are used to identify periods of financial turbulence that could impact economic stability and inform policy responses.  Calculated as the sum of standardized subcomponents.

descriptions.en: Quantitative measures that signal the level of stress in the financial system. codes.name: Herfindahl index
codes.description: A measure of market concentration and competition, calculated as the sum of the squares of the market shares of all firms in the market.

descriptions.en: A measure of market concentration and competition, calculated as the sum of the squares of the market shares of all firms in the market.

codes.name: Harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP)
codes.description: The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) gives comparable measures of inflations for the countries and country groups for which it is produced. It is an economic indicator that measures the change over time of the prices of consumer goods and services acquired by households.  In other words, it is a set of consumer price indexes (CPIs) calculated according to a harmonized approach and a set of definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations. For example, the European Union's HICP provides the official measure of consumer price inflation in the euro area for the purposes of monetary policy and the assessment of inflation convergence as required under the Maastricht criteria for accession to the euro.

descriptions.en: The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) gives comparable measures of inflations for the countries and country groups for which it is produced. It is an economic indicator that measures the change over time of the prices of consumer goods and services acquired by households.  In other words, it is a set of consumer price indexes (CPIs) calculated according to a harmonized approach and a set of definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations. For example, the European Union's HICP provides the official measure of consumer price inflation in the euro area for the purposes of monetary policy and the assessment of inflation convergence as required under the Maastricht criteria for accession to the euro.

codes.name: Industrial production index (IPI)
codes.description: Industrial Production Index (IPI) is a monthly economic indicator that measures changes in the volume of output in the industrial sector, typically comprising manufacturing, mining, and utilities.

codes.name: Import price index

codes.name: Nominal effective exchange rate (NEER)
codes.description: A nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports.

descriptions.en: A nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports.

codes.name: Price deflator
codes.description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels.  Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms.

descriptions.en: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels.  Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms.

codes.name: Producer price index (PPI)
codes.description: The Producer Price Index (PPI) is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.

descriptions.en: The Producer Price Index (PPI) is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.

codes.name: Real effective exchange rate (REER)
codes.description: A real effective exchange rate (REER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies divided by a price deflator or index of costs. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports. An increase in REER implies that exports become more expensive and imports become cheaper; therefore, an increase indicates a loss in trade competitiveness.

descriptions.en: A real effective exchange rate (REER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies divided by a price deflator or index of costs. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports. An increase in REER implies that exports become more expensive and imports become cheaper; therefore, an increase indicates a loss in trade competitiveness.

codes.name: Retail sales index
codes.description: The Retail Sales Index (RSI) measures the monthly performance of the retail sector by tracking changes in the value of sales at retail establishments. It is an important economic indicator that reflects consumer spending and retail sector health, providing insights into economic trends and consumer behavior.

descriptions.en: The Retail Sales Index (RSI) measures the monthly performance of the retail sector by tracking changes in the value of sales at retail establishments. It is an important economic indicator that reflects consumer spending and retail sector health, providing insights into economic trends and consumer behavior.

codes.name: Financial price index
codes.description: A composite index that tracks the movement of financial asset prices, such as stocks, bonds, and other securities. It provides insights into the overall performance of financial markets and can signal shifts in investor sentiment, economic expectations, and market conditions.  Calculated as one unit equivalent to one standard deviation of standarized variable.

descriptions.en: A composite index that tracks the movement of financial asset prices, such as stocks, bonds, and other securities. codes.name: Stock returns
codes.description: Measures the profit or loss generated on an investment in a stock over a specific period. Stock returns can be calculated based on price appreciation (capital gains) and any dividends received, offering investors a comprehensive view of the performance and profitability of their stock investments.

descriptions.en: Measures the profit or loss generated on an investment in a stock over a specific period. codes.name: Theil index
codes.description: A Theil index can be interpreted as a measure of redundancy, lack of diversity, isolation, segregation, inequality, non-randomness, and compressibility.  In the context of diversification, the higher the index the less diversification.

codes.name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) under EDP

names.en: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) under EDP

codes.description: Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually  equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

descriptions.en: Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually  equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

codes.name: Public or Unrestricted
codes.description: Information that has been published in full by the Fund and has been approved to be made available inside and outside the Fund without restriction is “Public” or “Unclassified.”

descriptions.en: Information that has been published in full by the Fund and has been approved to be made available inside and outside the Fund without restriction is “Public” or “Unclassified.”

codes.name: For official use only
codes.description: Information that is intended for all staff, without restriction, and in some cases, may be shared with national officials or other authorized individuals or institutions must be classified “For Official Use Only.” This may be information not authorized for public use but to which staff members may have access without demonstrating a particular direct interest in the matter in question. Such information must be marked accordingly when necessary to avoid being mistaken for unclassified information.

name: Frequency
description: This code list provides a set of values indicating the "frequency" of the data (e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly). The concept “frequency” may refer to various stages in the production process, e.g. data collection or data dissemination. For example, a time series could be disseminated at annual frequency but the underlying data are compiled monthly. The code list is applicable for all different uses of "frequency". This code list was formally adopted on 4 December 2013. More information about and supporting material for this code list and SDMX code lists in general (e.g. list of generic codes for expressing general concepts like "Total", "Unknown", etc.; syntaxes for the creation of further codes; general guidelines for the creation of SDMX code lists) can be found at this address: https://sdmx.org/?page_id=4345.

codes.name: Occasional annual
codes.description: The event occurs occasionally with an infrequent update that could span from 1 year to several years between events. It implies a survey that experiences a gap for several years prior to the next survey update (this is commonly linked to funding available to run a specific survey (i.e. health surveys), whereas a regular annual survey refers typically to ‘programs’ that are funded regularly and fall under the Statistics Act, and therefore never experience a gap)

name: Derivation Type
description: This codelist identifies the specific method used to derive a new data element or indicator from source data, such as raw data, IMF staff calculations, IMF staff estimates, or IMF staff projections.

descriptions.en: This codelist identifies the specific method used to derive a new data element or indicator from source data, such as raw data, IMF staff calculations, IMF staff estimates, or IMF staff projections.

codes.name: Raw data (no derivation)
codes.description: Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

descriptions.en: Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

codes.name: IMF Staff calculations (derived value)
codes.description: Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

descriptions.en: Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

codes.description: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

codes.name: IMF Staff estimates
codes.description: Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

descriptions.en: Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

codes.name: IMF Staff projections
codes.description: Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.

descriptions.en: Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.

codes.name: Mixed-type data
codes.description: Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.

descriptions.en: Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.

description: This codelist indicates if there is a potential overlap in the coverage of a particular indicator with another indicator in other datasets published by the IMF.

name: Valuation
description: This codelist defines refers to the rules and conventions used for recording monetary flows and stocks in macroeconomic statistics. Standard national accounts valuations include the basic price (what the seller receives) and the purchaser's price (what the purchaser pays). The purchaser's price is the basic price, plus taxes less subsidies on products, plus invoiced transportation and insurance services, plus distribution margin. International trade in goods considers the free on board (fob) price and cost-insurance-freight price, among others. Other valuation types include prices used in financial markets (e.g., buy and sell prices).

descriptions.en: This codelist defines refers to the rules and conventions used for recording monetary flows and stocks in macroeconomic statistics. Standard national accounts valuations include the basic price (what the seller receives) and the purchaser's price (what the purchaser pays). The purchaser's price is the basic price, plus taxes less subsidies on products, plus invoiced transportation and insurance services, plus distribution margin. International trade in goods considers the free on board (fob) price and cost-insurance-freight price, among others. Other valuation types include prices used in financial markets (e.g., buy and sell prices).

codes.name: Nominal value
codes.description: Outstanding amount that at any moment in time the debtor owes to the creditor. It reflects the funds originally advanced, plus any subsequent advances, plus interest that has accrued, less any repayments (2016 MFSMCG definition).

descriptions.en: Outstanding amount that at any moment in time the debtor owes to the creditor. It reflects the funds originally advanced, plus any subsequent advances, plus interest that has accrued, less any repayments (2016 MFSMCG definition).

codes.name: Market value
codes.description: The price at which an asset would change hands if it sold on the open market. Market prices for transactions are defined as amounts of money that willing buyers pay to acquire something from willing sellers; the exchanges are made between independent parties and on the basis of commercial considerations only, sometimes called “at arm’s length.”

descriptions.en: The price at which an asset would change hands if it sold on the open market. Market prices for transactions are defined as amounts of money that willing buyers pay to acquire something from willing sellers; the exchanges are made between independent parties and on the basis of commercial considerations only, sometimes called “at arm’s length.”

codes.name: Face value
codes.description: The amount of principal to be repaid (for example, the redemption amount of a bond). Sometimes called initial contractual value, for loans, the face value is the original amount of the loan as stated in the loan contract. If the loan is not fully disbursed, then the face value will include future disbursements, just as the face value of a zero-coupon bond includes interest that has not yet accrued.

descriptions.en: The amount of principal to be repaid (for example, the redemption amount of a bond). Sometimes called initial contractual value, for loans, the face value is the original amount of the loan as stated in the loan contract. If the loan is not fully disbursed, then the face value will include future disbursements, just as the face value of a zero-coupon bond includes interest that has not yet accrued.

codes.name: Book value
codes.description: Valuation used in business accounts, generally referring to the value recorded in the enterprise records. Book values may have different meanings because their values are influenced by the timing of acquisition, company takeovers, frequency of revaluations and tax and other regulations.

descriptions.en: Valuation used in business accounts, generally referring to the value recorded in the enterprise records. Book values may have different meanings because their values are influenced by the timing of acquisition, company takeovers, frequency of revaluations and tax and other regulations.

codes.name: Fair value
codes.description: Valuation that reflects the market-equivalent value of an asset or liability. It is defined as the price at which an asset could be exchanged, or a liability settled, between knowledgeable, willing parties in an arm's-length transaction.

descriptions.en: Valuation that reflects the market-equivalent value of an asset or liability. It is defined as the price at which an asset could be exchanged, or a liability settled, between knowledgeable, willing parties in an arm's-length transaction.

codes.name: Factor cost
codes.description: Gross value added at factor cost is derived by subtracting "other taxes, less subsidies, on production" from gross value added at basic prices.

descriptions.en: Gross value added at factor cost is derived by subtracting "other taxes, less subsidies, on production" from gross value added at basic prices.

codes.name: Cost insurance freight (CIF)
codes.description: The c.i.f. price (i.e. cost, insurance and freight price) is the price of a good delivered at the frontier of the importing country, including any insurance and freight charges incurred to that point, or the price of a service delivered to a resident, before the payment of any import duties or other taxes on imports or trade and transport margins within the country.

descriptions.en: The c.i.f. price (i.e. cost, insurance and freight price) is the price of a good delivered at the frontier of the importing country, including any insurance and freight charges incurred to that point, or the price of a service delivered to a resident, before the payment of any import duties or other taxes on imports or trade and transport margins within the country.

codes.name: Free on board (FOB)
codes.description: The f.o.b. price (free on board price) of exports and imports of goods is the market value of the goods at the point of uniform valuation, (the customs frontier of the economy from which they are exported).  It is equal to the c.i.f. price less the costs of transportation and insurance charges, between the customs frontier of the exporting (importing) country and that of the importing (exporting) country.

descriptions.en: The f.o.b. price (free on board price) of exports and imports of goods is the market value of the goods at the point of uniform valuation, (the customs frontier of the economy from which they are exported).  It is equal to the c.i.f. price less the costs of transportation and insurance charges, between the customs frontier of the exporting (importing) country and that of the importing (exporting) country.

codes.description: A debt instrument with a fixed interest rate and valued at its face value (the amount to be repaid).
